questions.question: What is the main disadvantage of First Come First Served (FCFS) scheduling for elevators?
options: It cannot handle multiple elevators
It causes excessive back-and-forth travel between distant floors
It does not support door open/close operations
It requires too much memory to store requests
questions.explanation: FCFS processes requests in arrival order regardless of floor proximity. This causes the elevator to zigzag between distant floors, dramatically increasing wait times and travel distance compared to directional algorithms.

questions.question: How does the SCAN algorithm schedule elevator movement?
options: It always goes to the nearest requested floor first
It moves in one direction servicing all requests, then reverses direction
It randomly selects which floor to visit next
It prioritizes floors with the most waiting passengers
questions.explanation: SCAN moves the elevator in one direction (up or down), servicing all pending requests along the way. When it reaches the end of the shaft, it reverses direction. This is why it's also called the 'elevator algorithm' in disk scheduling.

questions.question: What improvement does LOOK provide over SCAN?
options: LOOK uses multiple elevators simultaneously
LOOK reverses direction at the last request instead of at the end of the shaft
LOOK adds priority handling for emergency floors
LOOK reduces the door open/close time
questions.explanation: LOOK improves on SCAN by reversing direction as soon as there are no more requests in the current direction, rather than traveling all the way to the top or bottom floor. This eliminates unnecessary travel beyond the last request.

questions.question: Which design pattern best models the different operational states of an elevator (idle, moving up, moving down, door open)?
options: Observer pattern
State pattern
Factory pattern
Decorator pattern
questions.explanation: The State pattern is ideal for modeling an elevator because behavior changes based on current state. Each state (Idle, MovingUp, MovingDown, DoorOpen) encapsulates its own transition logic and behavior, avoiding complex conditional chains.

questions.question: In a multi-elevator system, how does the dispatcher typically decide which elevator to assign to a hall call?
options: It always assigns the elevator with the lowest ID number
It evaluates estimated time of arrival based on position, direction, and load
It assigns elevators in a round-robin fashion
It always assigns the elevator closest to the ground floor
questions.explanation: A smart dispatcher calculates a cost for each elevator based on current position, travel direction, pending stops, and passenger load. The elevator with the minimum estimated arrival time or cost is assigned to the request.

questions.question: What happens in fire mode for an elevator system?
options: All elevators speed up to double their normal speed
A designated elevator overrides all requests and returns to the ground floor
All elevators stop at the nearest floor and open doors
The system switches to FCFS scheduling for fastest response
questions.explanation: In fire mode, a designated elevator cancels all pending requests and moves directly to the ground floor (or a designated recall floor). Other elevators may also be recalled. This is a safety requirement codified in building codes.

questions.question: Which relationship best describes how a Building, Floor, and Elevator relate in a class diagram?
options: Building inherits from Floor, Floor inherits from Elevator
Building has composition with Floors and aggregation with Elevators
Elevator inherits from Building
Floor and Elevator have no relationship
questions.explanation: A Building owns Floors (composition — floors cannot exist without the building) and contains Elevators (aggregation). The Elevator traverses Floors but is a sibling entity to Floor within the Building, not a child of Floor.

questions.question: In a system with 4 elevators, elevator A is at floor 3 going up with stops at 5 and 8, elevator B is idle at floor 10, and a request comes from floor 6 going up. Which elevator should the dispatcher choose?
options: Elevator B because it is idle
Elevator A because it is already heading up and will pass floor 6
A new elevator should be allocated
The request should be queued until an elevator becomes free
questions.explanation: Elevator A is already moving upward and will pass floor 6 between its stops at 5 and 8. It can pick up the passenger with minimal detour. Elevator B would need to travel from floor 10 down to 6, which is a longer trip.

questions.question: Why is the Observer pattern useful in an elevator system?
options: It allows elevators to observe and copy each other's behavior
It lets the display panels and dispatcher subscribe to elevator state changes
It enables elevators to observe passenger weight
It allows the building to observe weather conditions
questions.explanation: The Observer pattern lets multiple components (floor displays, dispatcher, logging systems) subscribe to elevator events like position changes and door states. When an elevator changes state, all observers are notified without tight coupling.

questions.question: How can you prevent starvation in elevator scheduling, where a request on a low-traffic floor is perpetually skipped?
options: Use FCFS scheduling exclusively
Implement aging — increase request priority based on wait time
Disable multi-elevator coordination
Limit the building to two floors
questions.explanation: Aging gradually increases the priority of older requests. If a floor-2 request has been waiting for a long time while the elevator services busy upper floors, its priority eventually rises high enough to be serviced next, preventing indefinite starvation.
